sections.html:
Kokomo anchors Howard County, a north central Indiana county of 293.92 square miles. It is the seat of government and the biggest city, with Greentown, Russiaville and Indian Heights as the other names you hear. The 2020 census put the population at 83,658, and about 74 percent of residents live in urban areas.

Manufacturing, automotive work in particular, is the backbone of local employment. Stellantis runs a transmission plant, the Indiana Transmission plants and a casting plant here, a Kokomo engine plant started production in 2022, and StarPlus Energy, a joint venture of Stellantis and Samsung SDI, is in town as well. Many households rely on a handful of plants, so plant news moves housing demand.

Tornadoes have left their mark. On April 11, 1965 an F4 storm hit south Kokomo and killed 25 people in the area. Two tornadoes hit the north side on April 20, 2004. On August 24, 2016, an EF3 tornado damaged about 1,000 homes on the south side and destroyed 80.

Yearly averages are 44.4 inches of precipitation and 34.1 inches of snow. Leftover storm damage, an aging roof or a half-finished repair will turn up at the appraisal and the buyer's inspection. Either fix it first or expect to discount for it.

Look for all three tax offices inside the Howard County Administration Center at 220 North Main Street, Kokomo. Each is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

  • Assessor, 765-456-2211: assessed values, Form 130 appeals and exemption applications on Form 136.
  • Auditor, 765-456-2215 (tax line 765-456-2216): homestead deduction filings and tax sale listings.
  • Treasurer, Room 226, 765-456-2213: bills, payments, delinquent lists, and weed, demolition and nuisance liens.

The treasurer takes payments online through InvoiceCloud, at four local banks and through the drop box beside the Administration Center door. Partial payments are accepted. For a reassessment question, call the assessor, who is working through eastern Howard County starting with Taylor Township.

Certified rates for taxes payable in 2026 run from about 1.80 in rural Clay Township to about 3.75 inside the Kokomo city district that overlaps Taylor Township. Each rate is stated per $100.00 of taxable property.

Tax districtTotal rate per $100.00
Clay Township1.7992

Kokomo City, Harrison Township3.7142
Kokomo City, Center Township3.7234
Kokomo City, Taylor Township3.7452

More than twenty districts exist, so match the district code on your tax bill to find yours.

Your rate does not tell you what you will pay. Indiana also puts a ceiling on each parcel, measured against its gross assessed value.

  • Homestead with the standard deduction: 1 percent
  • Other residential, such as a single-family house without a homestead claim or a building with two or more dwelling units: 2 percent
  • Agricultural land: 2 percent. Nonresidential and personal property: 3 percent

Legislation passed in 2025 phases the standard homestead deduction down: $48,000 for the 2025 assessment date, $40,000 for 2026, $30,000 for 2027 and $0 from 2030 on. A supplemental homestead deduction grows over the same years, starting at 40 percent for taxes payable in 2026 and reaching 66.7 percent in 2031.

Sign and date a homestead application by December 31. One filing carries forward year to year until the property is sold, the title changes or the contract is paid off. A buyer therefore has to apply on their own, since the seller's deduction stays behind.

An appeal begins with Form 130, one petition for each parcel, delivered to the assessing official. June 15 is the cutoff, but the year follows the notice. A Form 11 mailed ahead of May 1 means June 15 of that assessment year. A later mailing means June 15 of the year your bill is sent.

The assessor first sets a preliminary informal meeting and then reports back to the county board. You should get a board hearing within 180 days of filing, announced by mail at least 30 days early. Dissatisfied, or still waiting after 180 days? File Form 131 with the Indiana Board of Tax Review.

Two points favor the owner. When the value jumped by more than 5 percent from the prior assessment date, the assessor has to prove it, unless renovation, new improvements or a change in use caused the jump. And paying on last year's assessment during the appeal is penalty free until the case ends.

Two installments come due each year, in May and in November. Pay up to 30 days late on a parcel with no back taxes and you owe 5 percent. After that, or with back taxes, it is 10 percent of the unpaid tax.

Bills run a year behind: what you pay now reflects ownership and value on January 1 of the prior year. A closing in the middle of the year can therefore leave the buyer covering a prorated piece of the seller's arrears. The closing agent works out the split.

sections.h2: Unpaid taxes and the tax sale
sections.html:
Delinquent parcels are offered at a yearly tax sale held in the Commissioners' Meeting Room, with a possible switch to online bidding. The minimum bid covers back taxes and special assessments, the current sale-year taxes, penalties, $25 for postage and publication, and county costs. Even after a sale the owner can redeem:

  • 110 percent of the minimum bid if redeemed within six months, or 115 percent after that
  • Plus any overbid amount and 5 percent yearly interest on it, plus taxes the buyer paid afterward
  • For certificates sold at the 2026 sale, the redemption period ends October 27, 2027. Certificates struck to the county may end February 24, 2027.

Paying the taxes by cash, cashier's check or credit card removes a parcel from the certified list.

sections.h2: What to gather before selling with tax due
sections.html:
Line up the paperwork before any buyer asks. The treasurer will quote what a parcel owes, and the closing agent settles it out of your proceeds.

  • Your latest tax bill and the parcel number
  • Any Form 11 assessment notice and any Form 130 you filed
  • Whether the parcel appears on the certified tax sale list
  • Records of weed cut, demolition or nuisance liens the treasurer has placed
  • Your homestead deduction approval, if you claimed one

Verify each figure by phone first. Cash sales skip lender delays and repair requests, though the tax still comes out of your proceeds.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Howard County, Indiana?
faqs.a: The Howard County Treasurer, at 220 North Main Street, Room 226 in Kokomo, collects property tax and can be reached at 765-456-2213. Questions about value or a missing homestead deduction go to the assessor or auditor.

faqs.q: When are Howard County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Installments are due each May and November. Partial payments are accepted, and you can pay online, at a participating bank or in the drop box.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Howard County taxes late?
faqs.a: The state's schedule adds 5 percent for payment within 30 days of the due date on a parcel with no back taxes, and 10 percent of the unpaid tax after that.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Howard County assessment?
faqs.a: File Form 130 with the assessor by June 15 of the year tied to your notice, one form per parcel. If the county board's decision is unsatisfactory, Form 131 goes to the Indiana Board of Tax Review.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Howard County house that is on the tax sale list?
faqs.a: Yes. Paying the taxes takes the parcel off the certified list, or the closing agent pays them from proceeds. After a tax sale, an owner can still redeem, and for certificates sold at the 2026 sale that period ends October 27, 2027.
